parts.title: The parrot who came to stay
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When my grandfather moved to a small flat last spring, he could not take his parrot with him. The landlord did not allow pets, and Pepper, who is thirty years old and bright green, needed a new home. My parents said that he could stay with us for a few weeks. That was eight months ago, and nobody has mentioned him leaving since.

At first, I was not happy about it. Pepper talks, and not only in a polite way. He copies the sound of the doorbell, the washing machine and my mother's mobile phone, so the whole family keeps running to answer things that do not exist. He also learned to say "Dinner's ready!" in my father's voice, which is very confusing when you are hungry.

However, I slowly began to enjoy his company. In the afternoons, when I came home from school, the house was always silent, and Pepper would shout "Hello, you!" as soon as he heard my key. I started to talk to him about my day. He cannot give advice, of course, but he is a very patient listener, and sometimes he says "Really?" at exactly the right moment.

Last week, my grandfather called to say that his new landlord had changed his mind about pets. He asked if we would like him to take Pepper back. My whole family said no at the same time, and my mother was the first.

questions.prompt: Why did Pepper come to live with the writer's family?
options: Her grandfather could not keep him.
He had been ill for some weeks recently.
Her parents had always wanted a pet.
questions.explanation: The landlord of the grandfather's flat did not allow pets, so Pepper needed a new home.

questions.prompt: What was the problem with the way Pepper talked?
options: He copied sounds that confused the family.
He said rude words to the visitors who came.
He only spoke at night when everyone was asleep.
questions.explanation: He copies the doorbell, the washing machine and phones, so the family run to answer things that do not exist.

questions.prompt: How did the writer's feelings change?
options: She began to teach him new words.
She enjoyed having a listener at home.
She became angry with her father.
questions.explanation: She started to talk to Pepper about her day and appreciated that he was a patient listener.

questions.prompt: What happened when Pepper's owner phoned last week?
options: He asked for a few more weeks of time.
He offered to send Pepper's food.
He said he could take Pepper back.
questions.explanation: The grandfather said his new landlord had changed his mind and asked if the family wanted him to take Pepper back.

questions.prompt: How did the family react to the offer?
options: They argued about it for days.
They asked to keep him for longer.
questions.explanation: They all said no at the same time, which means they refused straight away.

parts.title: Dogs that work
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There is one extra sentence.
parts.passage:
Many people think that dogs are simply pets, but some dogs have a very serious job. Assistance dogs help people who have problems seeing, hearing or moving. [1] The training takes about two years, and it begins when the puppies are only a few weeks old.

At first, the puppies live with volunteer families. [2] They learn to walk calmly on a lead, to sit quietly in shops and to ignore food on the floor. These lessons are not easy for a young dog.

At about twelve months, the dogs move to a training centre. [3] For example, a dog may learn to open doors, pick up a dropped phone or press the button at a pedestrian crossing.

Not every puppy passes the course. [4] Some are too nervous, and others find it hard to stay calm near traffic. These dogs are not failures: most of them find loving homes as family pets.

When a dog finally meets its new owner, the first meeting is often emotional. [5] "It changed my life," says one owner. "I go out on my own now."
sentences: Trainers teach them useful tasks that match each owner's needs.
Their job is to give the dogs experience of everyday life.
Some dogs also work for the police.
The dogs must also like working and be happy to learn.
Within weeks, the two usually become a close team.
These clever animals are trained to be calm and to obey many commands.

gaps.explanation: "Assistance dogs help people..." leads to sentence F, which explains how the dogs are trained to be calm and obey commands; the next sentence is about the training.
"The puppies live with volunteer families" is followed by their job: to learn about everyday life, which links to the lessons that follow.
"The dogs move to a training centre" leads to trainers teaching useful tasks; the next sentence begins "For example".
"Not every puppy passes" continues with other conditions: the dog must like the work, and the next sentence gives reasons why some do not.
The first meeting with the owner is followed by what happens within weeks, and then by the owner's comment on how it changed life.

parts.title: Why do cats purr?
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: Most people believe that cats purr when they are happy, and that is often [1]. A cat that is lying on your knee and feels safe will usually purr. However, cats also purr in other situations. Vets have noticed that some cats purr when they are in [2], or even when they are afraid. Scientists think that purring may help cats to feel better, because the gentle sound [3] a kind of comfort. Mother cats purr to guide their kittens, which are born blind and cannot [4] their mother's face. Many cats also learn to use purring to get what they want. They make a special, higher sound [5] they are hungry, and owners find it difficult to ignore. It is not [6] to tell what a purr means, but it is always interesting to listen.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "That is often true" confirms that cats purr when they are happy.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: Vets have seen cats purr when they are in pain; this fits the idea of comfort in difficult situations.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: The sound "gives a kind of comfort" means it provides comfort.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: Newborn kittens are blind, so they cannot recognise their mother's face.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "When they are hungry" says the time that the special sound is made.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: The writer means it is not easy to understand the meaning of a purr.

parts.title: Thinking about a puppy
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Mum and Dad,
I know you said that we cannot have a dog, but please read this before you decide. I have looked [1] the shelter website, and there is a small puppy called Mochi who needs a home. I promise to walk him [2] day before school and to clean up after him. The garden is big enough for him to play [3], and he will be good company when I am alone. If you say yes, I will use my pocket money to buy [4] own food and toys. I have already asked Grandma, and she has offered to look after him [5] we are on holiday. Please think about it, [6] I will do anything you ask!
Love, Nico

gaps.explanation: We say "look at a website"; "on" is also possible with a website.
We play in the garden: the preposition shows the place.
The possessive adjective refers to the puppy: his food and toys.
"When we are on holiday" gives the time that Grandma will look after him.
"And" adds the promise to do anything they ask.

parts.title: An interview with a wildlife rescuer
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Perdita, you run a rescue centre for wild animals. How did it start?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Quite by accident. Ten years ago, I found a baby hedgehog in my garden, and it was very weak. I took it to a vet, who showed me how to look after it. Soon, other people began to bring me animals that they had found.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What kind of animals do you get?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Mostly hedgehogs, birds and the occasional fox. In the summer we also get a lot of young birds that have fallen out of nests.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Should people pick up an animal when they find it?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Not always. If it is a baby bird with feathers, its parents are probably nearby. The best thing is to watch from a distance. We only need to be called if the animal is injured or in the road.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the hardest part of your work?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Saying goodbye. I look after the animals for weeks, and I get attached to them. But the aim is always to put them back in the wild, so I know I've done my job well when they run away from me.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Do you have any help?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Twenty volunteers. Some of them are teenagers who come after school, and they're very good with the animals. Yesterday one of them taught a nervous young fox to drink from a bottle.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you like people to do?

turns.speaker: perdita
turns.text: Put out a shallow bowl of water in their gardens in hot weather. It is such a simple thing, but it saves many animals.
